epic_title: Architecture, boundaries, testability and release quality
summary: ARCH defines module boundaries, test seams, and release gates. User-visible behaviour belongs to the other epics.

stories.title: Layered architecture with a single allowed dependency direction
stories.story: As a maintainer extending Calendaric, I want the codebase organized into layers with one allowed dependency direction, so that I can change one concern without having to understand or risk breaking the others.
stories.rationale: The map shows the old code mixing note IO, date parsing, settings resolution and UI inside single files, and reaching into other plugins' internals from three separate layers at once.

acceptance_criteria.given: a module in the view layer (calendar rendering, settings tab, modals)
then: it imports only from the domain layer and from interfaces that layer defines for date, note, and settings logic
it contains no import of the vault-IO adapter layer
it contains no import of the cross-plugin-integration layer
acceptance_criteria.evidence: src/arch.test.ts "AC-ARCH-01.1: no module outside src/main.ts constructs an adapter" -- its KNOWN_DEBT list is now empty, so the assertion is that adapterWiring(EDGES) reports nothing at all. Settled by US-ARCH-11, which moved the four remaining constructions (src/ui/calendar.ts and src/ui/calendarDots.ts) into src/main.ts behind a CalendarDeps object. The checker is proved able to fail by the sibling case "AC-ARCH-01.4: a new view-to-vault-IO import fails the check, named by file and by import", which feeds it a synthetic src/ui/newPane.ts -> src/adapters/obsidianVaultAdapter.ts edge and requires it to be reported.

acceptance_criteria.given: the domain layer (period and date logic, template-token resolution, settings validation)
then: it contains no import of the "obsidian" package
it contains no import of any adapter module or any view module
acceptance_criteria.evidence: src/arch.test.ts 'AC-ARCH-01.2: imports nothing from "obsidian" at runtime' and 'AC-ARCH-01.2: imports no adapter module and no view module', over every domain module the tree classifier finds (src/fmt/*, src/notes/*, src/commands/*, src/types.ts, src/settings/model.ts, dailyNotesImport.ts, importSource.ts); `import type` is read as type-only and allowed, which is what the domain uses for Command and for every port. Mutations, re-measured after the US-MIG-05 rebase: added 'import { Notice } from "obsidian";' to src/types.ts -- 32 passed -> 1 failed | 31 passed -> restored 32 passed; added 'import { ConfirmationModal } from "../ui/modal";' to src/notes/noteUtils.ts -- 32 passed -> 1 failed | 31 passed -> restored 32 passed.

acceptance_criteria.given: the plugin lifecycle module where dependencies are connected
then: it is the only module allowed to import from every layer
no other module imports the plugin lifecycle module
acceptance_criteria.evidence: src/arch.test.ts 'AC-ARCH-01.3: src/main.ts imports from every layer', 'AC-ARCH-01.3: no other module imports from every layer' and 'AC-ARCH-01.3: nothing imports the lifecycle module at runtime'. src/main.ts reaches view, domain, port, adapter and integration; no other shipped module reaches all five. Three modules import the plugin class as a TYPE (src/settings.ts, src/settings/dailyNotesImportCard.ts, src/ui/CalendarView.ts) -- erased before the bundle exists, so no runtime edge and no cycle. Mutations, re-measured after the US-MIG-05 rebase: deleted main.ts's ObsidianCompanionPluginAdapter import -- 32 passed -> 1 failed | 31 passed -> restored 32 passed; turned src/ui/CalendarView.ts's 'import type CalendaricPlugin' into a runtime 'import CalendaricPlugin' -- 32 passed -> 1 failed | 31 passed -> restored 32 passed.

acceptance_criteria.given: a change introduces an import from the view layer into the vault-IO layer
then: the check fails
the check names the offending file and the disallowed import
acceptance_criteria.evidence: src/arch.test.ts 'AC-ARCH-01.4: a new view-to-vault-IO import fails the check, named by file and by import' runs the same derivation (adapterWiring) over the real edge set plus one synthetic view->vault-IO import, and requires the report to differ from the recorded list and to contain 'src/ui/newPane.ts -> src/adapters/obsidianVaultAdapter.ts' -- the offending file and the disallowed import, both named. Mutation on the real tree, re-measured after the US-MIG-05 rebase: added 'import { ObsidianVaultAdapter } from "../adapters/obsidianVaultAdapter";' to src/ui/cellActions.ts -- arch.test.ts 32 passed -> 1 failed | 31 passed -> restored 32 passed, and the failure message printed that file and that import.

acceptance_criteria.given: any layer other than the cross-plugin-integration layer needs information about a companion plugin (Periodic Notes, Templater, or any other)
then: it is obtained only through a typed function exported by the integration layer
no other layer imports a companion plugin's module directly
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Re-derived after US-MIG-05 landed, which broke the first version of this check twice. (a) The integration layer is now DERIVED, not named: it is src/adapters/companionPluginPort.ts plus every src/adapters/ module importing it, so obsidianPeriodicNotesAdapter.ts classifies as integration on its own and a fourth companion adapter will too. (b) The surface scan no longer matches a bare id literal, which had fired on src/settings/importSource.ts, where '{ source: "periodic-notes" }' is a discriminant tag and the plugin is reached through PeriodicNotesPort -- correct code reported as a violation. It now matches the plugin REGISTRY (internalPlugins, .plugins, ["plugins"], getPlugin/getPluginById) or an id used AS a lookup (indexed with, passed as a call argument, or compared against), never an id sitting after ':' or '|'. Tests: 'AC-ARCH-01.5: no layer but the integration layer looks a companion plugin up', 'AC-ARCH-01.5: the lookup patterns tell a lookup from a tag' (four lookup forms must match, three tag forms must not), 'AC-ARCH-01.5: every other layer takes the port, never the adapter' and 'AC-ARCH-01.5: the port exports typed operations and nothing untyped' (asserted by shape, so a sibling adding operations does not break it). Four mutations, all on the post-rebase tree: registry hop '(window as unknown as Record<string, unknown>)["plugins"]' added to src/notes/periodicNoteIndex.ts -- 32 passed -> 1 failed | 31 passed -> restored 32 passed; id comparison '=== "periodic-notes"' added to src/settings/model.ts -- 32 passed -> 1 failed | 31 passed -> restored 32 passed; src/settings/importSource.ts made to import ObsidianPeriodicNotesAdapter instead of taking the port -- 32 passed -> 3 failed | 29 passed -> restored 32 passed; and the derived membership itself, by stripping the companionPluginPort import out of obsidianPeriodicNotesAdapter.ts so it falls back to the vault-IO layer -- 32 passed -> 1 failed | 31 passed -> restored 32 passed.

acceptance_criteria.given: the codebase makes any desktop-only API call (an Electron or Node capability not available on mobile)
acceptance_criteria.when: its imports and call sites are inspected
then: every desktop-only import and call is confined to one named adapter boundary
view modules and settings modules depend only on that adapter boundary's interface, never on the desktop-only API directly
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The repository does make one desktop-only call: a settings link opened the format guide through (window as any).require("electron").shell.openPath and read the desktop-only vault adapter's basePath, both inline in src/settings.ts. Moved behind one named boundary: src/adapters/desktopShellPort.ts (DesktopShellPort.openPluginFile) and src/adapters/electronDesktopShellAdapter.ts, constructed in src/main.ts and handed to the settings tab as a port. src/arch.test.ts 'AC-ARCH-01.6: one module holds every desktop-only import and call' scans every shipped module for require("electron"), FileSystemAdapter, basePath, node: builtins, child_process, __dirname and process.* and requires the hit list to be exactly [electronDesktopShellAdapter.ts]; 'AC-ARCH-01.6: the view depends on that boundary's interface, never on the API' requires src/main.ts to be its only runtime importer. Mutation, re-measured after the US-MIG-05 rebase: added a require("electron") call to src/ui/calendarNav.ts -- arch.test.ts 32 passed -> 1 failed | 31 passed -> restored 32 passed.

stories.title: One implementation per shared concept
stories.story: As a maintainer, I want each date-parsing rule, filename-matching rule, and shared type defined exactly once in the codebase, so that fixing or extending a rule requires exactly one change instead of several coordinated ones.
stories.rationale: The map's most repeated finding is duplication: a date/time template-token pattern copy-pasted across five note-creation functions, two independently-diverging prefix-match implementations across the source repositories, a dev-plugin-id detection probe duplicated at six call sites across four functions in two repos, and (inside the target repository itself) a period-granularity type declared three times independently.

acceptance_criteria.given: day, week, month and year make up the first release's supported set of period granularities, and quarter is a reserved value that is not part of that release set
acceptance_criteria.when: that set is declared as a type
then: exactly one module owns the declaration
the declaration names quarter as reserved rather than as a supported release granularity
every other module that needs the type imports it from that one module
no module independently redeclares an equivalent type

acceptance_criteria.given: a filename needs to be parsed into a date, whether by strict matching or by prefix-tolerant matching
acceptance_criteria.when: two different granularities or two different call sites need that parsing
then: both call the same shared parsing function
no second, independently-maintained parsing routine exists in the codebase

acceptance_criteria.given: a date or time template token is resolved for a note
then: it executes through one shared token-resolution function
no granularity has its own copy of the resolution logic

acceptance_criteria.given: the plugin needs to detect whether a companion plugin or feature is present
then: it exists in exactly one function that every caller uses
no second inline copy of the same detection logic exists elsewhere in the codebase

acceptance_criteria.given: a second implementation of a parser, a matcher, a shared type, or a detection routine is added anywhere in the codebase
acceptance_criteria.when: a duplication check runs over the source
then: the check flags the duplicate before the change can merge

decisions.title: The first release supports day, week, month and year; quarter is reserved
decisions.decision: The set of granularities the first release supports is day, week, month and year. Quarter is a reserved value: the type may name it and configuration may round-trip it, but no command is generated for it, no note is created for it, and no view offers it. Anything asking for quarter behaves the same way as any other granularity that is not enabled.
decisions.rationale: ARCH called quarter supported, NOTE used it as the example of an unsupported granularity, ICE-01 deferred it, and CMD still listed it for generated commands and startup opening. An agent reading the backlog could not tell whether quarter paths must work. This vault has quarter disabled, so nothing is lost by reserving it.

stories.title: Testable without a running Obsidian
stories.story: As someone maintaining Calendaric, I want the logic that decides what happens — not only pure date math — to be verifiable by an automated test, so that a change to note creation, settings resolution, or cross-plugin detection is checked by a test run instead of a manual reload-and-click pass.
stories.rationale: The target repository currently tests only pure functions; everything that touches the Obsidian API is untested, and its test double covers only three classes. Other epics list failure paths — a missing folder, an invalid format, a file that already exists, an absent template, an unparseable date — that this epic's testing seam must make reachable.

acceptance_criteria.given: a function that decides what note to create, open, or update
acceptance_criteria.when: it needs data from the vault or the app
then: it receives that data through an interface passed to it as a parameter or dependency
a test can supply a substitute for that interface without touching a real Obsidian instance
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/notes/noteCreate.test.ts, src/notes/noteOpen.test.ts — createNote/openNote/openNoteInNewTab now take VaultPort/WorkspacePort instead of the raw Obsidian App; all covered by FakeVaultPort/FakeWorkspacePort.

acceptance_criteria.given: the substitute used to stand in for the vault and workspace in tests
acceptance_criteria.when: a test exercises vault or workspace behaviour
then: the substitute covers every capability the plugin actually calls: file read, file write, file creation, workspace pane opening, and companion-plugin lookup
no capability the plugin calls is left uncovered by the substitute
acceptance_criteria.evidence: FakeVaultPort/FakeWorkspacePort cover file read/write/create and workspace pane opening (src/notes/noteCreate.test.ts, src/notes/noteOpen.test.ts). Companion-plugin lookup is already exercised without a running Obsidian by the pre-existing src/settings/dailyNotesImport.test.ts (its own hand-rolled App substitute, predating this ticket) — the capability is not left uncovered, though it is not yet unified under this ticket's VaultPort/WorkspacePort shape; that unification is US-ARCH-01/02 territory, not this ticket's.

acceptance_criteria.given: a named failure path (target folder missing, filename format invalid, note already exists at the target path, configured template absent, or date string unparseable)
then: a test exercises that failure path without a running Obsidian instance
the test asserts the observable outcome of that failure
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/notes/noteCreate.test.ts — 'creates the missing target folder', 'propagates the failure when a note already exists', 'creates an empty note when the configured template is absent', plus two seam-only proofs for 'invalid filename format' and 'unparseable date string' (FMT validation logic itself does not exist yet; these prove the port carries the rejection through).

acceptance_criteria.given: the domain layer's own test suite (period logic, template-token resolution, settings validation)
then: they execute with no dependency on the "obsidian" package, including its test double
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/arch.test.ts > "AC-ARCH-03.4: pure logic does not reach for the Obsidian API" — asserts that the import lines of templateTokens.ts, noteUtils.ts and noteDate.ts name no "obsidian" module. Mutation-checked: prepending an obsidian import to templateTokens.ts fails it. Supersedes the one-off grep this criterion rested on before.

acceptance_criteria.given: a change adds code that touches the vault, the workspace, or a companion plugin's API
acceptance_criteria.when: that change lands with no accompanying test exercising it through the substitute
then: the test-coverage gate for that layer fails
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Descoped by the orchestrator's own dispatch brief, section 5 (out of scope: building the automated CI coverage gate).
acceptance_criteria.not_applicable_because: Building an enforced, automated CI coverage gate for this criterion was explicitly out of scope for this ticket (orchestrator's own dispatch brief, section 5): a hand-written test alongside new vault-touching code satisfies the ticket procedurally. The automated gate itself is real follow-up work, not yet a story.

stories.title: One strict type-checking bar, with untyped externals walled off
stories.story: As a maintainer, I want the whole codebase held to one strict type-checking standard, with every place it touches an API the compiler cannot verify walled off behind a single typed boundary, so that a wrong assumption about another plugin's shape is caught while compiling, not when a user hits a crash.
stories.rationale: The target repository's tsconfig.json enables several of the strict-family flags individually but never sets the single "strict" option, and is missing others from that family. The old code reached into a companion plugin's internal state with a plain property read: one P1 defect read a Svelte store as if it were a plain object, and a feature it powered silently returned nothing for every user from the day it shipped.

acceptance_criteria.given: the TypeScript compiler configuration
then: strict mode is enabled as the single "strict" setting covering every strict sub-check
it is not a hand-picked subset of individually-enabled strict flags
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/arch.test.ts > "AC-ARCH-04.1: enables strict mode whole, never flag by flag" — reads tsconfig.json, requires strict:true, and requires that none of the nine strict-family sub-flags appears on its own. Mutation-checked: pinning strictNullChecks fails it.

acceptance_criteria.given: any function parameter, return value, or exported symbol in the codebase
then: no explicit or implicit "any" type is used to reach into a companion plugin's runtime object
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/arch.test.ts > "AC-ARCH-04.2: the companion-plugin boundary is typed, not `any`" — asserts companionPluginPort.ts and obsidianCompanionPluginAdapter.ts contain no ": any", "as any" or "<any>". Mutation-checked: adding a field typed any to the port fails it. Supersedes the one-off grep.

acceptance_criteria.given: the plugin needs data or a method from a companion plugin (Periodic Notes, Templater, or any other)
then: it is read only through a hand-written type describing the exact shape the plugin depends on
that type is defined in one place
every read of the companion plugin's state is validated or narrowed against that type before use
acceptance_criteria.evidence: code review: src/adapters/companionPluginPort.ts is the single definition of the depended-on shape and src/adapters/obsidianCompanionPluginAdapter.ts is its only reader. vitest: src/adapters/obsidianCompanionPluginAdapter.test.ts > narrows a well-shaped plugin to the depended-on fields, plus the narrowing suite around it (absent registry, registry that is not a record, missing getPluginById, non-object lookup result, receiver preservation).

acceptance_criteria.given: a companion plugin's object does not match the expected shape at runtime (a missing method, a state container that requires an accessor instead of a direct property read, or an absent property)
then: the read is detected as invalid and handled explicitly
the depending feature is either disabled visibly or reports an explicit error
it does not silently return an empty or wrong result while appearing to have succeeded
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/adapters/obsidianCompanionPluginAdapter.test.ts > a host that throws > reports a mismatch when getPluginById throws / > reports a mismatch when a property getter throws / > does not let the exception escape the adapter; plus > an enabled plugin whose shape does not match > reports a mismatch when enabled is not a boolean / > reports a mismatch when the disable method is missing, and the disabled-state suite. Each mismatch yields an explicit reason and decideDailyNotesCard returns unreadable rather than an offer, so no silently-empty success path remains. The remaining clause -- that the user actually SEES the notice -- is testable_by manual and unverified: renderUnreadableCompanionNotice has no DOM test, since the repo has no jsdom harness for the settings tab.

acceptance_criteria.given: the build runs the compiler in strict mode over every first-party source file
acceptance_criteria.when: a type error exists anywhere under the plugin's own source
then: the build fails
it does not merely emit a warning while completing successfully
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/arch.test.ts > "AC-ARCH-04.5: the type checker reads the tests too" — asserts tsconfig include covers src/**/*.ts, that no exclude entry names a test file, and that noUncheckedIndexedAccess stays on. Supersedes the orchestrator probe (injecting a type error into src/settings.test.ts and watching npm run build exit 2), which proved the same thing once and left nothing behind.

stories.title: Adding a granularity or a calendar indicator is a small, localised change
stories.story: As the person adding a new period type or a new calendar indicator later, I want that addition to touch a small, predictable set of files, so that extending Calendaric never means relearning or rewriting the whole plugin.
stories.rationale: In the target repository today, only day and week are functionally implemented anywhere; month, quarter, and year exist only as inert data shapes and permanently-disabled settings toggles. Separately, the old calendar-ui's indicator (calendar-source) contract was rewritten wholesale between two versions of the same library, forcing every one of its four real consumers to be rewritten rather than extended — the new contract must not repeat that failure mode.

acceptance_criteria.given: the set of supported period granularities
then: it requires one new entry in a single registry plus its own granularity-specific module
it requires no edit to the logic of any existing granularity's module

acceptance_criteria.given: the set of calendar indicators shown per day
then: it is implemented by one new module satisfying a documented indicator interface
it requires no change to the rendering code that already displays other indicators

acceptance_criteria.given: an indicator module written against the documented interface
acceptance_criteria.when: the interface changes in a later version
then: existing indicator modules either keep compiling unchanged, or fail to compile with a specific error naming the exact incompatibility
no existing indicator module changes behaviour silently at runtime as a result

acceptance_criteria.given: a new granularity or indicator is added and reviewed
acceptance_criteria.when: the change's file footprint is checked
then: it touches only its own new module, the single registry entry, and (for a granularity) that granularity's settings default
it does not touch the note-creation, parsing, or rendering logic belonging to an existing granularity or indicator

decisions.title: The indicator interface changes additively only
decisions.decision: Once published, the contract a calendar indicator implements only gains optional members. Removing or repurposing an existing member is a breaking change that requires a new contract alongside the old one.
decisions.rationale: The previous indicator contract was rewritten in a single version bump and broke every implementation at once. An additive-only rule is the cheapest guarantee that keeps that from repeating.

stories.title: A reproducible release build with every gate actually enforced
stories.story: As a release owner, I want one clean build to run every gate and produce every release artifact, so that releases are reproducible.
stories.rationale: AGENTS.md sets the manifest and versioning rules a release must satisfy. Elsewhere in the source material, the Periodic Notes fork had to drop lint from its build entirely because of a tooling bug, showing that a green build result does not by itself prove every gate ran. Separately, obsidian-daily-notes-interface needed a build-on-install script specifically so a consumer installing it directly from source would never silently receive unbuilt TypeScript in place of the compiled output.

acceptance_criteria.given: a clean checkout with only the pinned Node.js version installed
acceptance_criteria.when: the documented install-then-build commands are run
then: main.js, manifest.json, and styles.css (if present) are produced at the plugin root
no manual step beyond those commands is required
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/arch.test.ts > "AC-ARCH-06.1: one command produces a loadable plugin" — asserts npm run build is typecheck followed by the production esbuild run, that esbuild writes main.js at the plugin root, and that manifest.json carries an id and a version. Supersedes the orchestrator observation (deleted main.js, ran the build, 22040 bytes reappeared), which is not repeatable in CI.

acceptance_criteria.given: manifest.json's id and version, and versions.json, ahead of a release
then: manifest.json's id is unchanged from the previous release
manifest.json's version follows semantic versioning
versions.json records this exact version mapped to the same minAppVersion declared in manifest.json
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: scripts/release-check.test.mjs, the AC-ARCH-06.2 cases -- including > the re-release check reads a tag, not a same-named branch > passes when only a branch carries the version name / > still fails when a real tag for the version sits on another commit. That pair exists because the first implementation resolved an unqualified 0.1.0^{commit}, which a same-named branch can satisfy; it now resolves refs/tags explicitly. SemVer ordering and the versions.json-to-manifest mapping are covered in the same suite.

acceptance_criteria.given: a release has been tagged
acceptance_criteria.when: the release tag is compared against manifest.json
then: the tag matches manifest.json's version exactly, with no leading "v"
acceptance_criteria.evidence: UNSETTLED, reported rather than judged: the criterion is about a pushed tag matching manifest.json version with no leading v. The comparison logic is covered (scripts/release-check.test.mjs, the AC-ARCH-06.3 case), but no tag has ever been pushed on this repository -- the only tag present, 1.0.0, is inherited from the upstream template history dating to 2020. Settling this needs a real tagged release, deliberately not created here.

acceptance_criteria.given: manifest.json's minAppVersion for a release
acceptance_criteria.when: it is checked against the Obsidian APIs that release's code actually calls
then: a cited minimum-version source (Obsidian's own changelog or its API type definitions) justifies that minAppVersion
no API used by the release requires a newer Obsidian version than minAppVersion declares
acceptance_criteria.evidence: code review plus an independent check by the second-model reviewer, which verified the cited API references and version boundaries rather than taking them on trust. The floor is 1.13.7: the previous 0.15.0 was inherited from an old copy of the upstream sample plugin and never chosen for this project, while the code calls APIs requiring up to 1.7.2 (an awaitable revealLeaf, found reviewing US-CMD-01) and 1.1.0 (registerHoverLinkSource, found reviewing US-CAL-03) -- so the old value was actively false. 1.13.7 is the newest PUBLIC release, confirmed against obsidianmd/obsidian-releases desktop-releases.json, where latestVersion reads 1.13.7 and the beta channel reads 1.14.1. The 1.14.x line is Catalyst early access, not a public release, so it is not a target: naming it here would lock the plugin out of every non-Catalyst install. No bump is pending.

acceptance_criteria.given: the build runs type-checking, linting, and the test suite
acceptance_criteria.when: any one of those three fails
then: the build as a whole is reported as failed
none of the three is skipped, disabled, or allowed to fail while the overall build still reports success
acceptance_criteria.evidence: measured by the orchestrator: ran npm run verify and watched it report each gate individually -- gate typecheck: ok, gate lint: FAILED, gate test: ok -- and then exit 1 with "verify FAILED — 1 of 3 gates did not pass". No gate is skipped, disabled or allowed to fail while the run still reports success. The lint gate is red on a clean tree because of the pre-existing debt DEC-26 records, so a release stays blocked until that debt is paid; the failure output now says so explicitly, naming DEC-26 and telling the reader to compare counts on master before assuming they caused it. That blockage is the criterion working, not a defect -- whether lint should leave the release gate is a decision left to the repository owner.

acceptance_criteria.given: one of the three gates cannot run because of a tooling defect
then: the build fails loudly
the failure message names which gate could not run
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: scripts/verify.test.mjs, the AC-ARCH-06.6 case -- a gate that cannot run makes the build fail loudly and the message names which gate it was. Confirmed in the live run above, where the summary line names lint specifically rather than reporting a generic failure.

acceptance_criteria.given: the plugin or any of its internal packages is installed directly from source rather than from a published release
then: the built output it depends on is produced automatically as part of the install
a consumer never receives unbuilt source in place of the compiled artefact
acceptance_criteria.evidence: UNSETTLED, reported rather than judged: package.json declares prepare as npm run build, so an install does produce the built artefact, and the reviewer traced the npm lifecycle to confirm the ordering. But the criterion is about what a CONSUMER receives, and that can only be observed from a real install of a real published release -- nothing has been published from this repository yet.

stories.title: Handle changes to Obsidian UI and other plugin APIs
stories.story: As a Calendaric user, I want the plugin to keep working, or fail visibly, when Obsidian changes its own UI internals or a companion plugin changes its internal state shape, so that an Obsidian or Periodic Notes update never leaves my settings screen crashed or a feature silently doing nothing.
stories.rationale: Two P1 defects show why this matters. An Obsidian 1.13 change to the settings dialog crashed the Periodic Notes settings pane. Another integration read a state container as a plain object instead of using its accessor or subscription API, so a shipped feature always returned nothing.

acceptance_criteria.given: the plugin renders inside, or reads layout information from, an Obsidian-owned DOM element it does not control
acceptance_criteria.when: that element is absent or shaped differently than expected
then: the plugin skips the affected behaviour instead of throwing an unhandled error
no other part of the settings or view UI is left half-rendered as a result
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/settingsTabGuard.test.ts > "AC-ARCH-07.1: skips a section that throws instead of letting the error escape" / "AC-ARCH-07.1: leaves nothing half-rendered from the section that threw" / "AC-ARCH-07.1: renders every other section after one of them fails" / "AC-ARCH-07.1: names the skipped section rather than dropping it silently" / "AC-ARCH-07.1: guards each section separately, not the tab as a whole". The real display() runs under happy-dom with an Obsidian-owned surface broken: the import card half-draws and then throws, and separately Obsidian's own Setting class throws for the three sections that build rows with it. Mutation-checked twice on src/settings.ts. Neutering the rollback loop in renderGuardedSection ("while (containerEl.childNodes.length > before) {" -> "while (false) {"): 6 passed -> 2 failed | 4 passed -> 6 passed restored. Calling renderDailyNotesImportCard outside renderGuardedSection: 6 passed -> 4 failed | 2 passed -> 6 passed restored. Reachable from main.ts:65, which registers CalendaricSettingsTab.

acceptance_criteria.given: the plugin reads state exposed by a companion plugin (a settings object, a store, a cache)
acceptance_criteria.when: that state is a container that must be read through its accessor or subscription API, not as a plain object
then: the plugin reads it through that store's own subscription or accessor mechanism
the plugin never treats it as a plain object with a direct property read
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/adapters/obsidianCompanionPluginAdapter.test.ts > "AC-ARCH-07.2: reads a store's values through subscribe rather than as properties" / "AC-ARCH-07.2: subscribes with the container as the receiver" / "AC-ARCH-07.2: releases the subscription once it has the published value" / "AC-ARCH-07.2: reads a container that publishes through get() through get()". Mutation-checked on src/adapters/obsidianCompanionPluginAdapter.ts: making readStateContainer find no accessor ("ACCESSOR_KEYS.find((key) => typeof container[key] === \"function\")" -> "ACCESSOR_KEYS.find(() => false)"), which is exactly the plain-object property read the criterion forbids: 36 passed -> 8 failed | 28 passed -> 36 passed restored. Supersedes the two AC-ARCH-04.4 tests that refused an accessor-backed container outright rather than reading through it; every other shape AC-ARCH-04.4 names (missing method, absent instance, non-string value, throwing getter) is still refused and still tested.

acceptance_criteria.given: a companion plugin's internal state does not expose the value the plugin expects, because it was renamed, restructured, or the companion plugin is absent
acceptance_criteria.when: the plugin tries to read it
then: the read returns a typed "unavailable" result
the depending feature is disabled visibly, or falls back to a documented default
it does not silently no-op while presenting as enabled
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The typed result: vitest: src/adapters/obsidianCompanionPluginAdapter.test.ts > "AC-ARCH-07.3: returns a typed mismatch when the store publishes a non-record" / "AC-ARCH-07.3: returns a typed mismatch when subscribe publishes no value at all" / "AC-ARCH-07.3: returns a typed mismatch when get() hands back a non-record" / "AC-ARCH-07.3: the import card reads as unreadable, never as an offer". What the user sees: vitest: src/settingsCompanionUnavailable.test.ts > "AC-ARCH-07.3: tells the user the settings could not be read" / "AC-ARCH-07.3: names the documented fallback, which is entering them by hand" / "AC-ARCH-07.3: offers no import button that would store empty values" / "AC-ARCH-07.3: still offers the import when the store publishes readable values" -- the whole chain unmocked, from the registered settings tab down to the accessor read. This closes the clause AC-ARCH-04.4 left unverified for want of a DOM harness. Mutation-checked twice on src/adapters/obsidianCompanionPluginAdapter.ts, both times by reporting an unusable publication as an empty success (the mismatch return in readStateContainer -> "return { ok: true, value: {} };"), which is the silent no-op the criterion forbids: adapter test 36 passed -> 4 failed | 32 passed -> 36 passed restored; on-screen test 4 passed -> 3 failed | 1 passed -> 4 passed restored.

acceptance_criteria.given: a new version of Obsidian or a companion plugin changes a DOM structure or a data shape the plugin depends on
then: only the single adapter module written for that companion surface needs to change
no other module in the codebase reads that surface directly
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/arch.test.ts > "AC-ARCH-07.4: one module reads Obsidian's internal plugin registry" > "the adapter is the module that reads it" / "no other shipped module reads that surface directly" -- walks every shipped .ts under src/ (tests and __mocks__ excluded, because they stand in for the host) and requires the internalPlugins surface to appear only in src/adapters/obsidianCompanionPluginAdapter.ts. Mutation-checked on src/settings.ts by adding a second reader to display() ("void (this.app as unknown as Record<string, unknown>)[\"internalPlugins\"];"): 18 passed -> 1 failed | 17 passed -> 18 passed restored.

stories.title: User-facing documentation matches verified behaviour
stories.story: As a Calendaric user reading the format-and-template guide, I want every behaviour it documents to match what the plugin actually does, so that I can trust the documentation instead of discovering the real behaviour by trial and error.
stories.rationale: The map found docs/guide.md stating that week tokens follow the user's configured week-start setting, while the code that resolves those tokens hard-codes ISO week numbering regardless of that setting — the documented and the implemented behaviour disagree today.

acceptance_criteria.given: a behaviour described in the user-facing guide
then: a test asserts the documented behaviour directly
the guide and the code cannot silently diverge without a test failing

acceptance_criteria.given: the "Start week on" setting is configured to a given day
acceptance_criteria.when: a week-based template token or a week number is resolved
then: it uses the day configured in "Start week on", never a fixed numbering independent of that setting
the guide states that week-based tokens and week numbers follow the configured "Start week on" day

acceptance_criteria.given: the guide is opened from within the plugin's settings
then: the guide opens successfully on every platform the manifest declares support for
opening the guide does not depend on a desktop-only capability when the manifest declares mobile support

acceptance_criteria.given: a documented setting, command, or behaviour is renamed, removed, or changed
then: the guide is updated in the same change
it is not left for a later, separate pass

acceptance_criteria.given: the guide describes a setting, command, or behaviour that no longer exists in the current settings schema or command list
acceptance_criteria.when: the guide is checked against the current implementation
then: the mismatch is detected before the release ships
the guide is corrected, or the removed item is restored, before the release ships

decisions.title: Week-based tokens and week numbers follow the configured week-start day
decisions.decision: The user's 'Start week on' setting is authoritative for week numbering and for the {{monday:fmt}}..{{sunday:fmt}} tokens, in both the filename format field and the note body. ISO week numbering is not hard-coded. The two surfaces must resolve the same weekday to the same date for the same setting.
decisions.rationale: The existing documentation already promises this and the code contradicts it. Keeping the promise is the smaller change and the honest one. In this vault the setting is Monday-first, so ISO and configured agree today and no existing note is affected. This settles which rule is correct; the Sunday-start case is verified by AC-TPL-03.2 against a live Sunday-first vault, and that criterion stays unverified until someone runs it.

stories.title: A budget-aware GitHub Actions workflow enforces the release build's gates on every pull request
stories.story: As a release owner on a free-tier GitHub account, I want every pull request to run the same install, test and build gates automatically, so that a broken gate is caught before merge without relying on a human to run it locally, and without the workflow burning through a limited run-minute budget.
stories.rationale: No CI has ever run on this repository; ci.gates in the project's local tool config is provisional because it came from a local YAML parse rather than a real pipeline, and the account's Actions run-minutes are limited. Lint is deliberately excluded from the workflow at first — see DEC-26.

acceptance_criteria.given: a pull request is opened or updated against the default branch
then: it runs install, test and build as one combined job
it reports one status check on the pull request for that job
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/arch.test.ts > "AC-ARCH-09.1: the pull request gets one job and one status check" — asserts ci.yml declares exactly one job and that install, test and build are steps inside it. One job is what makes one status check. The observed run stands behind it: gh pr checks 6 reported a single check named "install, test, build", passing in 19s.

acceptance_criteria.given: the workflow's trigger configuration
then: it triggers only on pull_request events
it does not trigger on every push to a branch that has no open pull request
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/arch.test.ts > "AC-ARCH-09.2: runs on pull requests, not on every push" — asserts the on: block opens with pull_request and that no push trigger exists. Mutation-checked. Previously code review only, and listed in NO_REGRESSION_IDS; it has a regression behind it now and has left that list.

acceptance_criteria.given: any one of install, test or build fails during the workflow run
then: the status check reported on the pull request is failing
the workflow's own log names which step failed

acceptance_criteria.given: the workflow has completed at least one real run on a pull request
acceptance_criteria.when: the project's CI-gate detection is re-run afterward
then: it finds real pipeline or check-run data instead of falling back to a local YAML parse
the project's tool config can then be corrected from provisional to confirmed
acceptance_criteria.evidence: measured by the orchestrator: detect-ci-gates.sh re-run after the merge: source=github-checks (real check-run data, not the yaml-fallback path) — it picked up the most recent open pull request's check-runs rather than #6 specifically (default branch has no push-triggered checks by design), but this already confirms real pipeline data is reachable, matching gh pr checks 6 on #6 itself ("install, test, build" pass). ci.gates in .claude/stack.json can be moved from provisional to confirmed.

acceptance_criteria.given: eslint currently fails on the default branch itself, independent of any pull request's own changes (pre-existing debt, not introduced by this ticket)
then: it does not run lint as part of the pull-request gate
excluding lint is a deliberate, temporary choice, not a silent omission — DEC-26 states the reason and the exit condition
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/arch.test.ts > "AC-ARCH-09.5: runs no lint step, per DEC-26" — asserts no workflow step runs npm run lint or eslint. Mutation-checked: adding a lint step fails it. Previously code review only, and listed in NO_REGRESSION_IDS; it has a regression behind it now and has left that list.

decisions.title: The pull-request CI gate excludes lint until the pre-existing lint debt is paid down
decisions.decision: US-ARCH-09's workflow runs install, test and build, not lint. Every implementing agent must still run lint locally on its own worktree before reporting a ticket done. The 'zero new lint errors' requirement is judged by rule category, not raw count: a new instance of a rule already violated elsewhere in the codebase before this rewrite (chiefly no-restricted-imports on "import type { Moment } from 'moment'", and the existing no-misused-promises pattern on async event handlers) is accepted debt, same as the pre-existing 52; a genuinely new rule category never previously violated in this codebase is not excused by this decision and must be fixed before the ticket is done. That check stays a per-ticket discipline, not a CI gate, until a separate cleanup story pays down the existing debt. Once that debt is paid down, lint joins the CI gate in a follow-up change to this workflow.
decisions.rationale: eslint already fails on master with 52 pre-existing errors (mostly a no-restricted-imports rule against `import type { Moment } from "moment"`, tripped by code that predates this rewrite pass). Enabling lint in the CI gate today would make the very first pull request red regardless of its content. Anna's call: exclude it from CI for now (2026-09-11), because the debt is legacy, not because lint does not matter — hence the standing per-agent local-lint requirement.

stories.title: Take the upstream template's tooling improvements without losing the rewrite
stories.story: As a maintainer of a fork that has diverged deliberately from its template, I want the template's tooling improvements evaluated and taken one by one, so that the build and lint setup stays current without an upstream merge overwriting the plugin this project actually rewrote.
stories.rationale: This repository is a fork of obsidianmd/obsidian-sample-plugin and is three commits behind its fork point, touching 16 files. A plain merge is the wrong instrument: upstream's src/main.ts and src/settings.ts still hold the boilerplate sample, which a merge would drag back over the rewrite, and six of the sixteen files are ones this project has already diverged on on purpose (tsconfig.json via US-ARCH-04's strict mode, the deleted lint.yml replaced by US-ARCH-09's ci.yml, manifest.json and versions.json set to a real minAppVersion, and both source files). Only release.yml has been taken so far, verbatim, as a reference. What is left worth having is the tooling: the eslint plugin bump, which can move the pre-existing lint debt in either direction, and the esbuild and editorconfig modernisation.

acceptance_criteria.given: the fork's divergence from the upstream template
acceptance_criteria.when: each file the template changed since the fork point is examined
then: every one is classified as taken, superseded by this project's own work, or deliberately declined
each declined or superseded file carries the reason, so a later reader does not re-litigate it

acceptance_criteria.given: the upstream eslint plugin version is newer than the one this project pins
acceptance_criteria.when: the newer plugin is installed and lint is run
then: the resulting error count and the per-rule category breakdown are both recorded against the previous baseline
any rule category that appears or disappears is named, rather than only the total being compared

acceptance_criteria.given: the tooling changes chosen from the template
acceptance_criteria.when: they are applied to this repository
then: the test, build and lint gates all still pass
no file under src/ is reverted toward the template's sample-plugin content

acceptance_criteria.given: an upstream change that would overwrite work this project did deliberately
then: the build or the test suite fails rather than the overwrite landing silently
the failure names the file, so the cause is visible without bisecting

stories.title: The calendar view receives its vault access instead of constructing it
stories.story: As a maintainer changing how Calendaric reads the vault, I want the calendar view to receive vault access as an injected port rather than build its own adapter, so that I can swap or fake that access without editing the view, and so the layering rule holds in fact and not only in the import list.
stories.rationale: AC-ARCH-01.1 fails today: src/ui/calendar.ts constructs ObsidianVaultAdapter, ObsidianWorkspaceAdapter and ObsidianVaultConfigAdapter (lines 56-58), and src/ui/calendarDots.ts constructs ObsidianVaultConfigAdapter (line 21). The intent is already half-expressed -- calendarDots.ts:15 declares the field as VaultConfigPort and then assigns a concrete adapter to it, so the port exists and only the construction site is wrong. Removing the four imports alone would turn the criterion green while leaving src/ui/calendarDots.ts:43 and :66 calling app.vault.getAbstractFileByPath directly, which satisfies the letter of the boundary rule and none of its purpose. This story covers both halves. It cannot be expressed as a dependency of US-ARCH-01, because US-ARCH-01 is what waits on it.

acceptance_criteria.given: the calendar view modules (the calendar widget and the dot scanner)
acceptance_criteria.when: their constructors and fields are inspected
then: each vault, vault-config and workspace dependency arrives as a constructor parameter whose declared type is a port interface
neither module contains a `new` of any concrete adapter class
acceptance_criteria.evidence: arch.test.ts "AC-ARCH-11.1: no view module constructs or names a concrete adapter" and "AC-ARCH-11.1: the widget and the dot scanner take their ports as a constructor parameter". Mutation: calendarDots.ts constructor retyped to `private deps: ObsidianVaultConfigAdapter` -- both fail.

acceptance_criteria.given: a view module that needs to know whether a vault file exists or to react to a vault change
then: it obtains that information through an injected port, not through the Obsidian `App` object's vault surface
no view module calls `app.vault` directly for file lookup, creation, deletion or rename
acceptance_criteria.evidence: arch.test.ts "AC-ARCH-11.2: no view module reads the vault off the App object". Mutation: the day scan in calendarDots.ts put back to `this.app.vault.getAbstractFileByPath(path)` -- fails.

acceptance_criteria.given: the plugin lifecycle module, which is the only place allowed to know every layer
acceptance_criteria.when: the construction of the calendar view's dependencies is traced
then: every adapter the calendar view uses is constructed there and passed inward
the dependencies travel as one named dependency object rather than as separately threaded parameters, so adding a fifth port does not change three constructor signatures
acceptance_criteria.evidence: arch.test.ts "AC-ARCH-11.3: one named dependency object travels the whole calendar chain" and "AC-ARCH-11.3: the lifecycle module is where that object is built". Mutation: main.ts's `const calendarDeps: CalendarDeps` annotation dropped -- the second fails.

acceptance_criteria.given: a test that wants to exercise the calendar widget without a running Obsidian vault
acceptance_criteria.when: it constructs the widget with fake ports only
then: the widget renders and responds to a simulated vault change without any real vault being present
the test needs no monkey-patching of a module import to substitute the fakes
acceptance_criteria.evidence: calendarFakes.test.ts "AC-ARCH-11.4: renders and reacts to a vault change with fake ports only" -- FakeVaultPort/FakeVaultConfigPort/FakeWorkspacePort passed as constructor arguments, no module import patched. Mutation: DotScanner's onChange handler stripped of its onUpdate() call -- fails.

acceptance_criteria.given: a view module's port parameter is made optional, or is given a default that falls back to constructing a concrete adapter
acceptance_criteria.when: the project is type-checked and the architecture boundary check runs
then: the build fails and names the module and the dependency that was left unsupplied
no view module is able to reach a working vault without the lifecycle module having handed it one
acceptance_criteria.evidence: arch.test.ts "AC-ARCH-11.5: no view module makes a port optional or gives it a default", with a companion case proving it reports both shapes by module and dependency name. Mutation: calendar.ts's `private deps: CalendarDeps` made `private deps?: CalendarDeps` -- fails. The type checker is the other half: an unsupplied argument is a tsc error, `npm run build` exit 0.

notes: The two capability uids assigned to ARCH (forks:settings-tab-crash-guard-1.13, forks:git-dependency-self-build) are both single-defect fixes; every other criterion in this epic is derived directly from observations in calendaric-map.json rather than from a capability, per the schema's allowance for observation-derived criteria with covers left empty.

US-ARCH-05 (extensibility) and parts of US-ARCH-06 (release quality) are marked testable_by "manual" because verifying them means actually attempting the exercise (add a granularity, add an indicator, break a tooling gate) and reviewing the result's shape, not running an existing automated check.

tsconfig.json today enables several individual strict-family flags (noImplicitAny, noImplicitThis, strictNullChecks, strictBindCallApply, useUnknownInCatchVariables) but never sets the single "strict": true option, so it is missing others from that family (e.g. strictFunctionTypes, strictPropertyInitialization) implicitly. AC-ARCH-04.1 is written against the single-setting requirement rather than naming which flags are currently absent, since that list would go stale as the config changes.
No vault:* evidence-role capabilities were assigned to ARCH in epic-assignment.json, so no story carries a constrained_by entry.
